reason: E1 directly supports the premise that a single-phase solid solution without precipitates is weaker but more ductile, and that precipitation hardening increases strength at the cost of ductility, though in a different alloy system. E2 describes a eutectic structure with phase boundaries that achieves both high strength and ductility, which does not support the claim that phase boundaries necessarily reduce plasticity; this weakens the premise that nanoscale precipitates/ordered boundaries always cause a ductility loss. The hypothesis overgeneralizes from E1 and does not accurately represent E2'
premises: Single-phase solid solution without precipitates yields lower strength/hardness but higher ductility
Nanoscale precipitates or ordered phase boundaries act as effective dislocation obstacles, increasing strength/hardness and reducing ductility
The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates this strength–ductility trade-off in a different alloy system (AlCrFeTi-based) with precipitation-hardened conditions
The cited evidence (E2) shows that phase boundaries in a lamellar eutectic HEA can simultaneously achieve high strength and ductility, which is not directly aligned with the proposed trade-off
